"Compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world." - Albert Einstein

welcome
a note from Tim,

I love this quote. Einstein wasn't talking about the gym, but he might as well have been.


Compounding is a wondrous thing - and it isn't just for money. Health works the exact same way. It's not about showing up once a week, pushing so hard you can't move, and then disappearing for seven days to recover. That's not compounding - that's a single deposit with nothing behind it. Real results come from the small, boring, repeated deposits that stack on top of each other, week after week.

That's exactly why we built the Committed club.

A new feature dropped on the app last month that tracks it automatically: Show up 12+ times in a month and check in, and you're in. No shortcuts, no one-off heroics - just consistency, compounding,

QUICK TIP


​Don't start your day with coffee!


If you know me, your first thought is that I'm spouting some BS!
But, my first drink of the day is not a cup of coffee. That does not mean I haven't started the process for that delicious nectar of the gods to be in my hands!

What I start my day with is room temp water with electrolytes (sometimes just some mineral salt) and lemon juice - fresh squeezed if I'm feeling fancy - or from a jar (100% organic, not from concentrate) when i have to be at a 7am class for the early crew!

Your body starts a bit dehydrated after a night of rest - adding some salt or electrolytes allows your body to reset and the lemon can also be a good liver cleanse while the system is empty. Start your day with this if you don't already.

Once that is done - grab that coffee and enjoy!

Your numbers are feedback, not a grade. Track them so you can adjust — not so you can judge yourself.

Frozen greek yogurt berry bark

A refreshing, protein-packed summer treat made with greek yogurt, fresh berries, an a touch of natural sweetness. Perfect for hot afternoons and a healthier alternative to ice cream.

— 2 cups plaun Greek yogurt
— 1 cup strawberries, sliced
— 2 tbs honey (optional)
— 1/2 cup blueberries
— 1 tsp vanilla extract
— 1/2 cup raspberries
— 2 tbs chopped almonds
— 1 tbs unsweetened shredded coconut (optional)
— Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Instructions
1
Line a small baking tray or plate with parchment paper.
2
Mix the Greek yogurt, honey, and vanilla until smooth.
3
Spread into an even layer about 1/4-1/2 inch thick.
4
Sprinkle berries evenly across the yogurt
5
Add almonds and coconut.
6
Freeze for 3-4 hours, or until completely firm.
7
Break into pieces and enjoy straight from the freezer.
